title: Step 28 Bochner bounds horizontal twist
scope: Observation that Bochner also constrains the horizontal A-tensor

circle_bundle_decomposition.where: b = fiber bracket, φ = connection curvature (horizontal twist)
circle_bundle_decomposition.combined: Both bounds from the SAME Bochner identity

induction_consequence.quotient_Ricci_upper: Ric_B(X,X) = Ric_M(X,X) + 2|A_X U|² + T-terms. From two-sided pinching and ⟨|φ|²⟩ ≤ 4(Λ+δ): ⟨Ric_B(X,X)⟩_{|Z|²} ≤ (Λ+δ) + 2(Λ+δ) = 3(Λ+δ).
induction_consequence.remaining_gap: This is a WEIGHTED AVERAGE bound, not a POINTWISE bound. The induction needs pointwise Ricci control on the quotient. Averaging only gives quotient Ricci ≤ 3(Λ+δ) in the weighted L² sense. Passing to pointwise requires either Moser iteration on the quotient, or a different mechanism.
induction_consequence.partial_progress: The observation is that the horizontal twist IS controlled by Bochner (not a separate ingredient), just at the L² level. The gap is average-to-pointwise, not a missing bound entirely.

H3_model_check.note: In the H3 cohomogeneity-one model, the base is 1-dimensional, so there are no horizontal 2-forms and |A|=0. The entire |∇Z|² comes from fiber bracket (b²/2) and base variation (2k₃²). The horizontal twist bound is relevant for circle bundles over higher-dimensional bases, not for the codimension-one model.
